summary: Recorded the measured interpretation of the two-case control (CheckRun beca431464bf44ab9c3354145c21899f, exit 0, tests_passed), which isolates the cause of the snapshot-boundary loop. Both cases run the identical legal five-node history — a two-sided partition of {leader, partner} from the other three peers, the leader replicating uncommitted commands to the partner only, and a successor that commits its own entry at the first divergent index and snapshots there — and differ only in how much log the successor retains. TrailingLogs=0: precondition partner_store 1..7 at divergence_index 3 (index 1), successor snapshot at index 4 with its store fully compacted first/last 0 (index 2), and after the heal 687–697 InstallSnapshot installs with the partner's applied index pinned at 4 and its advertised last index stuck at 7 (index 9). TrailingLogs=3: the same precondition (index 11), the successor retaining 2..4 (index 12), and restores_before/early/late all 0 with the partner's applied and last index both at 4 (index 19). Conclusion violated, defect_claim asserted: once a leader has compacted past the boundary a rejoining follower needs, that follower cannot be repaired — it repeatedly receives the whole snapshot while its applied index stays at the snapshot index — because the rewind to the boundary yields ErrLogNotFound, replicateTo branches to SEND_SNAP, and the re-installed snapshot restores nextIndex to the boundary so the same rejection recurs. Retaining a few entries lets the leader walk the prev-log index into entries it still holds and the follower truncates its conflicting suffix normally. This also answers the outstanding reachability and cause gaps (precondition reached by real producers; compaction depth is load-bearing, not the partition or the snapshot). The Fact records the paired operands with the frozen-snapshot conditions, and the interpretation keeps the counterevidence (TrailingLogs=3 converges) and limitations (default 10240 not sampled, in-process transports, FSM-Restore-based counting, bounded ~1.5 s interval). Structural validation returned valid=true.
